title: What is Tokenization? Chunks vs. Individual Characters
text: The same topic, and it's fine. Same model, wildly different reliability. Here's why. The model doesn't read text one letter at a time. It reads chunks called tokens, sometimes a whole word, sometimes a word broken into a few pieces. A long or unusual word can get split in a way that has nothing to do with where its letters actually fall. The model sees the chunks. It never directly sees the letters inside them. title: Why LLMs Reconstruct Letters at the Wrong Resolution
text: Chunks. Ask the model to count a specific letter across the whole word, and it has to reconstruct the letters from chunks it never saw as individual characters. It's not lazy. It's working from the wrong unit entirely, and the count comes out wrong. Now, the fix that proves the mechanism. title: The Fix: Spelling Words Out Letter-by-Letter
text: Word changed. Only the unit it was working in did. Here's something to try today. Pick a long or unusual word. Ask an AI model to count a letter in it directly. Then ask it to spell the word out first one letter at a time and count again. If the second answer is more reliable than the first, you just watched tokenization in action.
